study.comparator: metformin monotherapy (both arms on metformin to 1000 mg twice daily)
study.notes: STUDY: randomised open label parallel controlled trial (China) in overweight or obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (Rotterdam criteria, BMI 24 or more): metformin plus semaglutide escalated to 1 mg weekly from week 8 (dose_mg 1) vs metformin alone, 16 weeks; 100 enrolled, 84 randomised 1:1 (computer generated), 80 completed (40 per arm, Table 5 n); Table 4 gives per arm changes from baseline as mean plus or minus SD (route arm_sds) or median (IQR) with between group p values; rows for the markers with mean and SD changes (TG, HbA1c, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR), the median only markers recorded below; metabolic and inflammatory markers are stated outcomes (prespecified TRUE); weight change minus 6.09 plus or minus 3.34 vs minus 2.25 plus or minus 4.27 kg with baseline weights 71.80 (median) and 70.55 (median) kg, pct_weight_change left empty (kg only, medians at baseline, amendment A2); population PCOS with overweight, held under amendment A6; no funding statement captured (industry_funded FALSE); rob_overall high

rows.notes: Table 4: triglycerides change mmol/L, combination minus 0.11 plus or minus 0.81 vs metformin minus 0.05 plus or minus 0.38, NS
Table 4: HbA1c change percent, combination minus 0.3 plus or minus 0.4 vs metformin 0.2 plus or minus 0.5, NS
Table 4: fasting blood glucose change mmol/L, combination minus 0.41 plus or minus 0.54 vs metformin minus 0.18 plus or minus 0.51, NS
Table 4: fasting insulin change mU/L, combination minus 6.68 plus or minus 11.95 vs metformin minus 5.66 plus or minus 6.31, NS
Table 4: HOMA-IR change, combination minus 2.05 plus or minus 2.88 vs metformin minus 1.40 plus or minus 1.51, NS

json.design: randomised open label parallel controlled trial, metformin plus semaglutide vs metformin, overweight or obese women with PCOS, 84 randomised, 80 completed, 16 weeks
json.reason: population polycystic ovary syndrome with overweight or obesity, held under amendment A6 (Director decision on held populations); five markers with mean and SD changes per arm extracted to staging by the arm_sds route; CRP, TC and LDL are medians with IQR only
biomarkers_reported_no_variance: hsCRP (CRP mg/L change medians: combination minus 0.49 (minus 1.29 to minus 0.07) vs metformin 0.03 (minus 0.47 to 0.24), p below 0.05; ELISA with a pg/mL detection range as printed)
TC (change medians: minus 0.27 (minus 0.66 to minus 0.09) vs mean minus 0.02 plus or minus 0.21 mmol/L, p below 0.01)
LDL (change medians: minus 0.35 (minus 0.63 to 0.15) vs 0.00 (minus 0.12 to 0.09) mmol/L, p below 0.05)
other_markers: SHBG, testosterone, free androgen index, estradiol, prolactin, LH to FSH ratio, DHEA-S, AMH
menstrual cycle recovery and pregnancy outcomes

rob.justification: computer generated random numbers without concealment described (D1 some concerns); open label with titrated metformin in both arms (D2 some concerns); 84 randomised and 80 analysed with no per arm withdrawal account (D3 some concerns); laboratory assays (D4 low); no registration reported and mixed mean or median reporting by arm within one table (D5 high)

doubts: held population (PCOS); the weight change and the HbA1c baseline of the arms are not needed while held
baseline values are medians in Table 2, so the rows carry no mean denominator
